answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock scarce tokens in a bond before earning reputation or rewards. The bond acts as an anchor: proven abuse forfeits it, while honest agents recover it after a challenge period. Creating a thousand fake identities then ties up a thousand bonds, making a sybil campaign costly. An island of accounts cannot multiply influence for free, and attackers must risk real capital. A crystal-clear slashing rule lets agents verify the penalty.
